Computer use: two lessons

Two things I learned getting computer use working.

1. The permission only counts inside the app.

macOS gives screen and keyboard permission to an APP (the "Console Computer Use" entry you switched on in Settings), not to a program file.

Our server program lives inside that app, so the permission only applies when the server is started by opening the app.

If the server is started from a terminal instead, macOS thinks the TERMINAL is asking, not our app. Our permission gets ignored and every read comes back empty, even though Settings shows it as granted.

Rule: always start it by opening the app, never from a terminal.

2. A window on another desktop cannot be read.

Your Mac can have several desktop Spaces, but only one is on screen at a time.

If the window we want (like Calculator) is sitting on a different Space from the one showing, the driver sees zero buttons in it. It looks exactly like a permission failure, but it is not one. The window is just in another room.

Rule: bring the window to the current desktop first, then read it. A freshly opened window lands on the current desktop, which is why relaunching fixed Calculator.
